newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat, Joradn's king criticise Israeli moves.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Joradn's king criticise Israeli moves.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein said on Saturday Israel's settlement plans in Arab East Jerusalem and its limited withdrawal from the West Bank threatened Middle East peace.

The two leaders met in Amman and discussed Israel's decision to build 6,500 Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem and its announcement on Friday that it would hand over only nine percent more of the West Bank in the first of three scheduled pullbacks, Jordan's Petra news agency said.

"The two sides affirmed these decisions which the Israeli government took violate international legitimacy which the peace process is based on, contradict the letter and the spirit of the agreements reached by the Palestinians and Israel, and form a threat to the whole peace process," it said.
Earlier on Saturday Arafat condemned a United States veto of a Security Council resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.

"It's a completely wrong decision," Arafat said after talks in Gaza with Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti. Washington used its veto on Friday to kill the resolution, supported by the 14 other Security Council members.

Arafat also called Israel's unilateral decision on the scale of its West Bank withdrawal "a trick and conspiracy", saying their peace deal called for the transfer of 30 percent of West Bank territory in each of the pullbacks.
